thread.title: Charting a second dead-cat bounce, S&P 500 rises from 10% correction mark - MarketWatch

author: Michael Ashbaugh
title: Charting a second dead-cat bounce, S&P 500 rises from 10% correction mark - MarketWatch
text:
Editor’s Note: This is a free edition of The Technical Indicator, a daily MarketWatch subscriber newsletter. To get this column each market day, click here.
Technically speaking, the U.S. benchmarks continue to whipsaw amid broadly bearish October price action.
Against this backdrop, the S&P 500 has failed a test of key resistance, miserably, as it continues to flirt with negative year-to-date territory under the 2017 close (2,673).
Before detailing the U.S. markets’ wider view, the S&P 500’s SPX, +1.28% hourly chart highlights the past two weeks.
See Also Apple iPad and Mac Event: The Highlights × As illustrated, the S&P has tagged five-month lows, extending the October plunge.
The downturn punctuates a failed retest of trendline resistance and the breakdown point (2,710). Monday’s session high (2,707) closely matched resistance.
Similarly, the Dow Jones Industrial Average has reached negative year-to-date territory.
In the process, the Dow has violated notable support matching the 2017 close (24,719), an area better illustrated on the daily chart.
Against this backdrop, the Nasdaq Composite has registered six-month lows.
The downturn punctuates a failed retest of trendline resistance closely matching the breakdown point (7,274).
Put differently, the Nasdaq’s near-term price action closely resembles that of the S&P 500.
Widening the view to six months, the Nasdaq is pacing its worst month since 2008 with just two October sessions remaining.
It continues to whipsaw amid less-charted territory. Tactically, deeper inflection points match the 2017 peak (7,004) and 2017 close (6,903).
Conversely, major resistance broadly spans from 7,474 to the 200-day moving average, currently 7,518. An eventual close higher would mark a step toward stabilization.
Looking elsewhere, the Dow Jones Industrial Average has extended to three-month lows.
Recall that trendline support closely matched the 2017 close (24,719). The index has notched consecutive closes under support, reaching negative year-to-date territory.
Deeper inflection points match the Dow’s 10% correction mark (24,256) and the June low (23,997).
Similarly, the S&P 500 has reached negative year-to-date territory.
The prevailing downturn punctuates a failed retest of the breakdown point (2,710) an area matching trendline resistance on the hourly chart.
The bigger picture As detailed above, a persistently damaging October downdraft remains underway. Consider that each big three U.S. benchmark has registered the following peak-to-trough downturn:
The Dow industrials have plunged as much as 2,830 points, or 10.5%, from the record peak established Oct. 3. The Nasdaq Composite has plunged as much as 1,210 points, or 14.9%, from the record peak established Aug. 30. The S&P 500 has plunged as much as 337 points, or 11.5%, from the record peak established Sept. 21. Put differently, each big three U.S. benchmark has already satisfied a 10% correction. (The Dow Jones Industrial Average has not yet closed in correction territory, under the 24,256 mark.)
Moving to the small-caps, the iShares Russell 2000 ETF has plunged to eight-month lows.
To reiterate, resistance spans from 152.46 to 153.00, levels matching the 2017 close and the breakdown point. A close higher would mark technical progress.
Similarly, the SPDR S&P MidCap 400’s October downdraft has inflicted extensive damage.
Tactically, notable overhead spans from 337.90 to 339.00, levels matching gap resistance and the breakdown point. The pending retest from underneath will likely add color.
Meanwhile, the SPDR Trust S&P 500 has registered five-month lows.
Tactically, major resistance matches the May peak (274.25) and is followed by the 200-day moving average, currently 276.30.
Against this backdrop, the S&P 500 has asserted a firmly bearish technical posture.
The October downdrafts have been directionally sharp — inflicting extensive damage — while the intervening rally attempt registered as flat. In essence, the S&P staged a lackluster defense of its 200-day moving average before selling off aggressively to five-month lows.
Tactically, familiar resistance matches the 2,710 breakdown point, detailed repeatedly. Monday’s session high (2,707) punctuated a failed retest from underneath, and the S&P subsequently plunged to new lows.
An eventual close atop the 2,710 area would mark a step toward stabilization.
On further strength, the May peak (2,742) is followed by the more distant 200-day moving average, currently 2,766. A close atop the 200-day moving average would raise the flag to a potentially legitimate market recovery attempt.
Conversely, deeper support, circa 2,605, (the November breakout point) is followed by the much deeper 2018 low (2,532).
Beyond specific levels, all technical trends — including the primary trend — remain bearish based on today’s backdrop. The October monthly close may add color.
See also: Charting an ominous technical tilt, S&P 500 plunges from the 200-day average.
See also: Cracks surface in the bull trend, S&P 500 nails major support.
Tuesday’s Watch List The charts below detail names that are technically well positioned. These are radar screen names — sectors or stocks poised to move in the near term. For the original comments on the stocks below, see The Technical Indicator Library.
Drilling down further, the Invesco QQQ Trust QQQ, +1.25% tracks the Nasdaq 100 Index and has broken down technically.
As illustrated, the QQQ has staged two strong-volume October downdrafts, violating trendline support and the 200-day moving average. The intervening rally attempt registered as comparably flat, fueled by decreased volume.
Tactically, resistance broadly spans from about 169.60 to 172.10, and an eventual close higher would place the brakes on bearish momentum. Monday’s session high punctuated a failed retest from underneath, and was met with pronounced selling pressure.
Familiar FAANG components pace the Nasdaq 100’s downdraft Moving to specific names, three familiar Nasdaq 100 components — Amazon.com, Alphabet, Inc. and Netflix, Inc. — have contributed to the benchmark’s breakdown.
To start, Amazon.com AMZN, -1.32% has turned lower, a downturn that accelerated last week after the company reported a third-quarter revenue miss, and guided its seasonally important fourth quarter firmly below consensus expectations.
In the process, the shares have violated the 200-day moving average amid a sustained volume spike. This marks Amazon’s first closes under its 200-day since March 2016 when the shares were then-priced around 554.
Tactically, Amazon’s intermediate- to longer-term bias remains bearish. (See the Oct. 17 review. ) An eventual close atop the 200-day moving average, currently 1,671, would mark a step toward stabilization.
Meanwhile, Alphabet, Inc. GOOGL, +1.13% has confirmed its primary downtrend. The prevailing leg lower has been punctuated by failed retests of the 50- and 200-day moving averages from underneath.
Here again, the October downturn accelerated, amid increased volume, after last week’s third-quarter revenue miss.
More broadly, notice the pending death cross, or bearish 50-day/200-day moving average crossover. An eventual close atop the 200-day, currently 1,135.70, and the slightly more distant breakdown point (1,159.40) would mark steps toward stabilization. (Also see the Oct. 17 review. )
Looking elsewhere, Netflix, Inc. NFLX, -1.04% has also asserted a bearish backdrop.
The prevailing downturn places the shares at six-month lows, punctuating a failed mid-October test of resistance despite the company’s strong third-quarter results.
More broadly, the October price action dovetails with a pending death cross, or bearish 50-day/200-day moving average crossover. Until this month, Netflix had not closed under its 200-day since September 2016.
Tactically, notable overhead broadly spans from about 321 to 333, and an eventual close higher would mark technical progress. (Also see the Oct. 22 review. )
Concluding with one stray note, the SPDR S&P Retail ETF XRT, +2.79% is showing near-term signs of stabilization.
Specifically, the group has averted a “lower low” in recent sessions, exhibiting relative strength versus the widely-tracked U.S. benchmarks. The pending retest of the 200-day moving average, currently 47.80, will likely add color.
Beyond near-term rally attempts, the group’s intermediate-term technical bias remains bearish pending repairs.
